en.title: EU proposes 45 billion euro loan for Ukraine to be repaid from Russian reparations
en.dek: European Commission proposes new 45 billion euro loan for Ukraine, split evenly between defense and state budget spending, to be repaid through future Russian war reparations.
facts: European Commission proposed a new 45 billion euro loan for Ukraine for 2027
The loan would be repaid through future Russian war reparations
The plan splits the funds evenly between defense and state budget spending
According to the Commission, the money would come from interest on the EU budget
Russia’s embassy in the Netherlands asked whether The Hague was openly joining the war after Dutch-headquartered defense company Destinus said its Ruta missiles struck the Crimean Bridge
The Dutch company confirmed the strike on the bridge linking annexed Crimea to Russia
body: The European Commission proposed a new 45 billion euro loan for Ukraine for 2027, to be repaid through future Russian war reparations, the Commission said the money would come from interest on the EU budget.
The plan splits the funds evenly between defense and state budget spending, according to the Commission.

Russia’s embassy in the Netherlands asked whether The Hague was openly joining the war after Dutch-headquartered defense company Destinus said its Ruta missiles struck the Crimean Bridge, a Dutch company confirmed the strike on the bridge linking annexed Crimea to Russia.
The Kyiv Post reported that Russia questioned the Dutch role in the Crimean Bridge strike, asking whether The Hague was openly joining the war.
The Dutch company Destinus confirmed its Ruta missiles struck the Crimean Bridge, the bridge linking annexed Crimea to Russia.
The European Commission's proposal represents the latest financial commitment from the EU to Ukraine amid the ongoing conflict.
The loan mechanism ties repayment to future Russian war reparations, creating a framework for funding Ukraine's needs from Russian assets.
en.context: The European Union has been providing financial support to Ukraine since the beginning of the Russian invasion, with this latest proposal representing a significant new loan mechanism tied to potential Russian reparations. The Dutch company Destinus confirmed a strike on the Crimean Bridge, a key infrastructure link between annexed Crimea and Russia, which Russia has questioned as potentially involving Dutch participation in the conflict.
